circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern circuit to join the Formula One calendar, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside the Supercars Championship Melbourne SuperSprint and various support categories. The venue maintains an FIA Grade 1 classification.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following renovations and a name change to the A1-Ring, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is an urban racing venue in Azerbaijan situated along Baku Boulevard, featuring a 6. 003 km lap that ranks as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first Middle Eastern Formula One Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual F1 race there alongside other motorsport events including GP2 Series and 24-hour endurance competitions. The FIA Grade 1 licensed track features multiple configurations and previously accommodated Australian V8 Supercars racing between 2006 and 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer facility serves as a versatile racing venue featuring a mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Ardennes region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7-kilometre circuit has hosted Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The Belgian Grand Prix has been a regular fixture on the calendar for nearly four decades, though it was absent in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: The Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer racing track located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, where the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix takes place annually. Beyond Formula One, the venue has hosted numerous international motorsport competitions including sports car championships and various racing series throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit is located in Jiading and serves as China's premier racing venue. It hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming from 2024, and has also begun hosting electric racing events from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated near villages in Northamptonshire that became the inaugural location for the British Grand Prix in 1948 and notably hosted the opening race of the inaugural Formula One World Championship in 1950. After alternating with two other British circuits during the 1955-1986 period, the championship event became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other contemporary Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after government authorities rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's main park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 and ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 with only one interruption, it remains one of Formula One's most enduring venues and earned its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its characteristic long straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometre Japanese motorsport facility in Mie Prefecture, operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track serves as a premier venue for both Formula One and Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its concentration of major hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates several of the city's most recognizable venues, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as it weaves through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City honoring two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned as a Formula One Grand Prix host in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now operating on a revised track configuration compared to its previous hosting periods which concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium in Florida, stretching 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, it joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the Miami Grand Prix annually.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of the principality, spanning 3. 337 kilometers around the harbor. Though officially named after Monaco itself, the circuit is popularly known as Monte Carlo since most of its layout traverses that particular neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until the partnership concluded in 2026. The venue, situated 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam close to the North Sea, marked Formula One's return to the Netherlands after a lengthy absence.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: This 4. 309 km Brazilian racing facility in São Paulo opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise circuit hosts major motorsport events and features a separate karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront, serving as the permanent home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The track has also begun hosting international electric racing events in recent years.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue in Singapore that winds through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts around Marina Bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of fast straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of driver and vehicle performance. With FIA Grade 1 certification and seating for approximately 140,700 spectators, the venue serves as a comprehensive racing facility in Catalonia, Spain.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The track hosts multiple major motorsport series including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship, alongside various other racing events throughout the year.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in the championship.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso represents Aston Martin in contemporary Formula One competition, bringing two world championship titles from his 2005-2006 stint with Renault and 32 career victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including multiple Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole competitor to win both the Formula One drivers' title and the World Endurance drivers' championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes. He has claimed eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently races for Haas in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One with the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that has yielded 10 race victories. He achieved runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship twice while driving for Mercedes, finishing as the title contender in both 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto has established himself in Formula One racing, currently competing for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver competing in European Le Mans Series LMP2 racing with Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One. The 2024-2025 season saw him participate in seven Grand Prix events for the team.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who represents France in Formula One competition, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently competes in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, Hülkenberg achieved significant success in endurance racing, securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monégasque driver Charles Leclerc races for Ferrari in Formula One, where he finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship. Throughout his nine seasons in the sport, he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who split his recent career between the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver and part-time NASCAR racing with Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One involvement spanned two separate periods, competing from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024 before transitioning to his current endurance racing focus.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren after competing in the series for eight seasons. He has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory with Alpine stands as a notable achievement in his racing career.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after spending 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 world championship while at Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One over 14 seasons from 2011 until 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport. Known by his nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from Formula One competition.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12 seasons in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in the IMSA championship for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda transitioned from a full-time Formula One career spanning 2021 to 2025 into a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag. Throughout his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in Formula One, currently fulfilling a reserve driver position with Cadillac. The Chinese racing driver competed in the sport's premier series from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole driver from his nation to have raced in F1.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021 under the Alpine brand, this team served as Renault's factory operation after being rebranded from its previous Renault F1 incarnation. The squad maintained its works status throughout its tenure before the French manufacturer withdrew from the championship following the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has a long-standing presence in Formula One through different corporate structures, with the modern iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding on the current grid.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished outfit, having participated in every championship season since 1950. The team, colloquially known by their horse emblem's nickname, maintains an unbroken presence in the sport that no other competitor can match.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR owner Gene Haas in 2014, debuting in the 2016 season, with Ayao Komatsu assuming the role of team principal in 2024 following Guenther Steiner's departure after leading the outfit since its inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing outfit founded in 1970, Sauber initially made its mark in endurance motorsport before joining Formula One in 1993. Throughout its three decades in the championship, the team underwent numerous restructurings before ceasing operations in 2025, having competed in more races than all but three other constructors in the sport's history. Audi acquired the team and its infrastructure in 2024 to establish the foundation for its own Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility, operating as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group structure and owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through team ownership and engine supply, with the current incarnation based in Brackley and holding a German licence. Following an ownership restructure completed in 2022, the team is now jointly held by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal shares. The squad carries the storied "Silver Arrows" nickname associated with Mercedes' racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second team. Based in Faenza with operational support from Milton Keynes, the outfit operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the energy drink conglomerate's two-team structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister outfit within the Red Bull F1 structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its 2005 establishment by Red Bull GmbH. The team, led by Christian Horner from its inception through 2024, was replaced in leadership by Laurent Mekies, while Red Bull GmbH also operates the separate Racing Bulls team in the championship.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team, the outfit operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters and has been a significant presence in the sport's history.
